title: Policy checks: reuse isolated jobs and authorized external or agent-provided services
body:
## Outcome

A native policy can obtain typed evidence from a deterministic sandboxed check or an authorized Service Gateway operation. The operator selects the implementation, dependencies and decision authority; the assessed workload cannot choose an arbitrary callback or supply its own authoritative result.

Parent: #1542. Shared result and decision semantics are owned by #1543.

## Implementation scope

Reuse `safeyolo job run`, its host-owned job definitions and existing isolation from #562. Support authorized service operations for external providers and agent-provided services. A policy reference resolves to an adopted service/capability/operation and owned input/output mapping, not an untrusted URL embedded in workload content.

Keep execution facts separate from the evaluator's findings. Exit zero means a process completed successfully; it does not mean the requested policy condition passed. Sandbox isolation constrains execution but does not establish a provider's accuracy. Delegating policy influence to an agent-provided or third-party service must be visible in the adopted configuration. Each selected operation declares whether it performs passive lookup, retains submitted data or can actively fetch/scan the subject; unknown effects cannot be presented as passive preview.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A named check runs through the existing job mechanism with host-selected executable/specification, bounded read-only inputs and a validated typed result. Host-observed execution/result provenance is retained; caller-written PASS text cannot stand in for it.
- [ ] A named check calls an authorized external service operation and an agent-provided operation through existing Service Gateway plumbing. Credentials and permitted operations remain scoped to the check's adopted dependencies. Tests prove that passive preview cannot accidentally submit an active scan; configured runtime checks retain their explicitly authorized behavior.
- [ ] Integration tests cover the gate-principal/provider identity seam: a transient job using stable `gate:<id>` authority can invoke an authorized agent-provided service with correct authenticated caller identity, without impersonating a configured workload agent or creating a durable fake agent.
- [ ] Dependency authorization is independent of the assessed destination. Missing grants and recursive/cyclic check dependencies produce explicit bounded failures; check traffic receives no blanket policy bypass.
- [ ] Deadlines, input/output limits, concurrent/pending work limits, cancellation and late-result handling are defined and tested. No network operation or VM startup occurs under a global policy lock. Execution failure, malformed results and provider unavailability remain distinct from negative findings.
- [ ] Repeated equivalent requests reuse valid evidence under the shared cache contract or deduplicate in-flight work. Tests or measurements show bounded cold and repeated-request behavior; a fresh full sandbox per URL is not the required default.
- [ ] A deterministic GitHub provenance example uses policy-owned expected identity and authoritative, captured GitHub evidence. It reports mismatch/unavailable separately and binds its finding to the exact issue content/revision consumed. Author identity alone does not attest comments or all content as safe.
- [ ] Existing job and service authority boundaries remain intact. Previously authorized ordinary calls do not generate recurring approvals, saved grants or persistent agent records per check execution.

## Scope and dependencies

#1543 defines the accepted result schema, precedence and policy influence. Execution work can start with that agreed contract and fixtures; closing this issue requires its runtime integration, not completion of every policy feature.

The GitHub example is a bounded reusable proof, not a factory admission redesign. Its expected owner/user comes from the operator's adopted policy, not a hard-coded project identity.

Reuse the current jobs/services implementations and existing operator interaction contract. A new microVM engine, always-on checker daemon, provider registry or separate approval service is not required. Hyperlight can remain a future implementation choice if measurements identify a need.

Planning estimate: L; uncertainty High, principally the transient gate-to-agent-provider identity path and bounded execution on installed native platforms.

## Baseline

- [Existing jobs](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/proxy/src/jobs.rs) and [delegated network authority](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/proxy/src/jobs/network.rs), delivered by #562.
- [Service routing](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/proxy/src/services.rs), [provider stream](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/proxy/src/provider_stream.rs) and [HTTP caller identity](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/proxy/src/http.rs). Current agent-provider routing expects a configured agent identity; external-service coverage alone does not prove the transient-job path.
- [GitHub helper reference](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/cli/src/safeyolo/agent_context/skills/safeyolo/references/github-checks.md) and [script](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/cli/src/safeyolo/agent_context/skills/safeyolo/scripts/github_checks.py), from #519: these consume caller-provided facts, and a failed comparison can still exit zero.
- [Native package build](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/blob/c9543b5c68fd86d218e61e32320864b337c52b9d/scripts/build_host_packages.sh): the historical GitHub helper/reference are not currently shipped in the native operator package.
